transcript:
Marcus Chen: Alright, let's jump into the platform migration update. We've got 30 minutes and I know everyone's calendar is packed, so let's be efficient. Priya, where are we on the data layer cutover?

Priya Sharma: Yeah, so, um, we've been making progress. I think we're in a pretty good place, actually. The team has been, you know, working through the schema migration scripts and I think we've gotten through maybe like 60 percent of the tables? It's hard to say exactly. There are some edge cases that are sort of tricky, but I think we can probably handle them. Hopefully by end of next week we'll have a better picture.

Marcus Chen: Okay. When you say 60 percent, is that 60 percent of the tables migrated and tested, or just scripted?

Priya Sharma: Um, scripted mostly. Testing is... we haven't really started the full integration test suite yet. We've done some spot checks. I was going to say, I think we might need to push the timeline a little bit? But I'm not sure by how much. Maybe a week? It's hard to tell right now.

Marcus Chen: That's concerning. Leadership is expecting a go/no-go decision on March 28th. If we're only 60 percent scripted with no integration testing, that feels like we're behind. What's blocking the testing?

Priya Sharma: Well, it's a few things. The staging environment has been flaky — DevOps is working on it but it keeps going down. And also, I think the team is a little stretched because we pulled two engineers onto the auth service incident last week. So basically we lost about 10 person-days.

Jordan Wells: I can speak to the staging issue. We identified the root cause yesterday — it's a memory leak in the connection pooler. We have a fix deployed to staging as of this morning. Should be stable now, but I'd want 24 hours of monitoring before we call it resolved.

Marcus Chen: Good. That helps. Priya, given that staging should be back, can you put together a revised timeline? I need something I can take to leadership that's honest about where we are.

Priya Sharma: Yeah, I can try to put something together. I mean, I think the issue is that there are a lot of unknowns still. Like, we don't know how long the edge cases will take until we actually dig into them. And I don't want to commit to a date that we might miss.

Marcus Chen: I understand the uncertainty, but we need to give leadership something. Even a range would be better than nothing. Can you give me a best-case and worst-case?

Priya Sharma: I guess best case would be... maybe April 4th for all scripts done and basic integration tests passing? Worst case, if the edge cases are really bad, maybe April 18th? But I really don't know. Those are sort of rough estimates.

Lena Kowalski: Can I jump in? I've been looking at this from the product side. We have three enterprise clients who were promised the new platform by end of Q1. If we slip to April 18th, that's a month past our external commitment. Have we thought about what we tell those clients?

Priya Sharma: That's a good question. I hadn't really thought about the client communication piece. I've been kind of heads down on the technical work.

Marcus Chen: That's fair, but it's something we need to address. Lena, can you draft a client communication plan for both scenarios — on-time and delayed?

Lena Kowalski: Already started one. I'll have it ready by Thursday.

Marcus Chen: Perfect. Jordan, the staging fix — is there anything the migration team needs to do differently once staging is stable?

Jordan Wells: No, they should be able to pick up where they left off. The connection pooler fix is backward compatible. One thing I'd flag though — we should probably set up dedicated staging monitoring for the migration window so we catch issues early rather than losing another week.

Marcus Chen: Agreed. Can you own that?

Jordan Wells: Yes, I'll have the monitoring dashboard up by end of day tomorrow.

Marcus Chen: Great. So to summarize — Priya, revised timeline by Wednesday. Lena, client comms plan by Thursday. Jordan, staging monitoring by tomorrow EOD. Let's reconvene Friday with a clear picture for leadership. Anything else?

Priya Sharma: I think we're good. I just want to say, I know this is behind where we wanted to be, and I'm sorry about that. The team is working really hard.

Marcus Chen: I appreciate that, Priya. No one's questioning the team's effort. We just need to get the communication to leadership right so we can manage expectations. Okay, let's wrap.
audience_context: Cross-functional status meeting with engineering lead (Marcus), DevOps lead (Jordan), and product manager (Lena). Marcus reports directly to the CTO and needs crisp updates to relay upward.
